MANUAL VERIFICATION

Manual Check

Verify any week independently.

Week 1 — timber properties

Verify f′b, f′t, f′c, f′s, E and E0.05.

Week 2 — tributary & beam

Area → line load → reactions → maximum moment.

Week 2 — modification factors

Directly verify the factor values selected in a solution.

Week 2 — wind check

Site speed and pressure.

Week 3 — tension capacity

Nd,t = φk1k4k6f′tAt.

Week 3 — tension deformation

δ = j3(NserviceL)/(AE).

Week 4 — S3 / S4 slenderness

Check both buckling axes.

Week 4 — compression capacity

Nd,c = φk1k4k6k12f′cAc.

Week 5 — spaced column geometry

A, Iy, radius, S5 and spacing checks.

Week 5 — governing capacity

Compare x, y and local-shaft modes.

Limit-state load combinations and critical case

AS/NZS 1170.0 Cl 4.2.2 — the first step of every strength question (Handbook Examples 3.4, 4.3, 5.7, 6.2). Enter the UNFACTORED action effects (all in the same unit: kN/m, kN or kN·m). Each combination takes the k₁ of its shortest-duration load; the critical case has the largest S*/k₁.

Week 6 — bending capacity

Verify Z, ρbS1, k12, Md and PASS/FAIL.

Week 6 — k9 strength sharing

Table 2.7 geometric factors + spacing relationship.

Week 6 — beam slenderness S1

Choose the restraint case used in the Week 6 lecture.

Week 8 — shear capacity

Vd = φk₁k₄k₆Asf′s with As = ⅔bd.

Week 8 — bearing capacity

⟂ grain uses k₇; ∥ grain has no k₇.

Week 8 — bearing at an angle θ

Nd,θ = Nd,pNd,ℓ / (Nd,ℓsin²θ + Nd,pcos²θ).

Week 8 — k₇ length of bearing

AS 1720.1 Table 2.6. Interpolates between listed lengths.

Week 8 — load found from the bending analysis

"For the load found in the analysis for bending strength…": the load that just uses up Md is w* = 8Md/L², then V* = w*L/2 and the bearing reaction N*p = V* (Handbook Ex 5.1).

Week 9 — beam deflection

δ = j₂ × elastic deflection, checked against a limit.

Week 9 — creep factor j₂

AS 1720.1 Figure 2.1, by duration and initial moisture content.

Week 9 — deflection for each serviceability combination

Each load component gets the creep factor of ITS OWN duration: δ = 5L⁴·Σ(j·w)/(384EI) (Handbook Ex 5.5–5.7). Permanent and long-term imposed parts use j₂; short-term parts use 1.0. Simply supported, UDL.

Week 10 — bending + compression

Both AS 1720.1 Cl 3.5 checks must pass.

Week 10 — bending + tension

Tension edge and compression edge, both required.

Week 10 — column capacities Nd,cx and Nd,cy

The combined-action equations need the compression capacity about EACH axis: Nd,cx uses S₃ = Lax/d and Nd,cy uses S₄ = Lay/b, each with its own k₁₂ (Handbook Ex 6.1–6.2).
